newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Cable firm plans 40 mln A share IPO.
newsitem.headline: China Cable firm plans 40 mln A share IPO.

text.p: Shandong Cable Electric Co Ltd plans to make an initial public offering of 40 million A shares in Shenzhen, a company spokesman told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin on Thursday.
The company will submit an application on the issue to China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) in April, the official said, but did not give a timetable for the offer.
Shandong Cable is one of 33 companies recently chosen by Beijing to list hard currency B shares.
The company plans to start preparatory work on the B share offer in 1998, he said. He gave no further details.
The firm, which sells most of its products domestically, would use proceeds to boost production of electric and telecommunication cables, the spokesman said.
The company has appointed China Securities Co Ltd as the main underwriter for the A share issue, he said.
The company, based in Taian city in the eastern province of Shandong, expects pre-tax profit to be 80 million yuan for 1997, compared with 68 million in 1996 and 50 million in 1995, he said.
Before the A share offer, outstanding share capital is 100 million, consisting of 61.1 million legal person shares, or shares held by institutions, and 38.9 million staff shares.
